lessons.title: Story Time: A Fire Safety Story
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about a fire-safety themed story.
success_criteria: I can answer a question about the story.
I can say what the character learned.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what children already know about fire safety.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a fire-safety themed story, modelling comprehension questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer questions about the story's events and message.
key_questions: What did the character learn about fire safety?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences with reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.plenary: Recap fire safety messages from the story.
lessons.home_link: Talk about your family's fire safety plan.

lessons.title: Addition Word Problems: Fire Station
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve addition word problems in a fire-station context.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition word problem.
I can show my working.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving a word problem (e.g. '5 firefighters are on duty, 3 more arrive, how many now?').
lessons.independent_task: Children solve 3-4 fire station themed addition word problems.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note word problem strategy use — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up a fire station addition problem for your family.

lessons.title: What Materials Can Catch Fire?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify materials that burn easily and those that don't.
success_criteria: I can name a material that burns easily.
I can name a material that doesn't burn easily.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what fire needs to burn (safely, without demonstration).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss (without any live fire demonstration) which materials are flammable (paper, wood) vs fire-resistant (metal, stone), using pictures/videos only.
lessons.independent_task: Children sort material picture cards into 'burns easily' and 'doesn't burn easily' with reasoning.
key_questions: Why do fire doors use certain materials?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain reasoning for material choices in fire safety equipment

lessons.assessment_notes: Note material property understanding applied to safety — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.home_link: Talk about fire-safe materials in your home (e.g. fire doors, smoke alarms).

lessons.title: Writing Fire Safety Instructions
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write simple fire safety instructions in order.
success_criteria: I can write a fire safety instruction.
I can use sequencing words.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap fire safety rules (stop, drop, roll; get out, stay out, call 999).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing simple sequenced fire safety instructions.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 3-4 fire safety instructions in order.
key_questions: What is the first thing to do?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note instructional writing and sequencing — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.home_link: Practise your family's fire escape plan.

lessons.title: Subtraction Word Problems: Fire Station
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve subtraction word problems in a fire-station context.
success_criteria: I can solve a subtraction word problem.
I can show my working.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving a subtraction word problem (e.g. '8 fire engines, 3 go out on a call, how many left?').
lessons.independent_task: Children solve 3-4 fire station themed subtraction word problems.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note word problem strategy use — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up a fire station subtraction problem for your family.

lessons.title: Testing Heat Resistance (Adult-Led Demo Only)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe what happens when materials are exposed to heat.
success_criteria: I can describe a change caused by heat.
I can say which material resisted heat best.
lessons.starter_activity: Predict what might happen to different materials near heat.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Adult-led safe demonstration only (e.g. warming materials gently, never open flame) showing heat effects; children observe from a safe distance.
lessons.independent_task: Children record observations from the demonstration, describing changes seen.
resources_needed: Safe heat source (e.g. warm water) for adult demonstration only

differentiation.support: Adult supports recording with picture prompts
differentiation.greater_depth: Explain why some materials resist heat better

lessons.assessment_notes: Note observational science skill in a safety-first context — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.home_link: Talk about heat-resistant materials used in the kitchen at home.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Fire Safety Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read fire-safety themed words.
success_criteria: I can blend and read safety words.
I can read a safety sentence.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/reinforce a grapheme, blending fire-safety themed words.
lessons.independent_task: Children read fire-safety themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading fire safety words over the week.

lessons.title: Telling Time: Fire Drill Schedule
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to read o'clock and half past times in a real-life context.
success_criteria: I can read the time on a schedule.
I can say what time an event happens.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap o'clock and half past from Week 4.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a simple 'fire drill schedule' with o'clock/half past times.
lessons.independent_task: Children read and answer questions about a fire-drill-themed schedule.
key_questions: What time is the fire drill?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record time-telling applied to a real context — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Read a schedule or timetable together at home.

lessons.title: Why Do Firefighters Wear Special Clothing?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explain why firefighters' clothing is made from special materials.
success_criteria: I can name a material firefighters wear.
I can say why it's suitable.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at pictures of firefighter clothing/equipment.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss the properties needed in firefighter clothing (heat-resistant, thick, protective).
lessons.independent_task: Children label a firefighter diagram with materials and their protective properties.
key_questions: Why does this material protect firefighters?

differentiation.support: Adult supports labelling with word bank

lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of material property knowledge to a real purpose — evidence for SCI.MAT.

lessons.title: Role-Play: Calling 999
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to speak clearly and calmly in a role-play emergency scenario.
success_criteria: I can say what the emergency is.
I can say my address clearly.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap what to say in a 999 call.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model a role-play 999 call, emphasising calm, clear speaking.
lessons.independent_task: In pairs, children role-play making and receiving a 999 call about a fire.

differentiation.support: Adult models the call, child repeats key info
differentiation.greater_depth: Role-play both caller and operator confidently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language clarity under a scenario — evidence for ENG.SL1.
lessons.plenary: Recap key information needed in an emergency call.
lessons.home_link: Learn your home address with an adult.

lessons.title: Counting in 2s: Fire Engine Wheels
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count in steps of 2.
success_criteria: I can count in 2s to 20.
I can use counting in 2s to count a set.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model counting in 2s using fire engine wheel pairs as a visual.
lessons.independent_task: Children practise counting in 2s to 20, applying it to count sets of paired objects.
key_questions: How many wheels on 3 fire engines?

differentiation.greater_depth: Count in 2s to 40+ and apply to problem solving

lessons.assessment_notes: Record skip-counting in 2s ability — evidence for MATHS.N1/N3.
lessons.home_link: Practise counting in 2s with pairs of objects at home.

lessons.title: Designing a Fire-Safe Material Poster
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to communicate fire-safe material choices in a poster.
success_criteria: I can name a fire-safe material.
I can explain why it's a good choice.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap fire-safe materials learned this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model planning a simple poster communicating fire-safe material facts.
lessons.independent_task: Children create a poster about fire-safe materials, including a picture and a fact.
key_questions: What fire-safe material will you feature?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of material science into a communicative product — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.home_link: Share your fire safety poster with your family.

lessons.title: Fire Safety Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about fire safety learned this week.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question about fire safety.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's fire safety vocabulary.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a short fire-safety passage, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: What does the passage say to do in a fire?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing
differentiation.greater_depth: Answer inference questions with full-sentence reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.plenary: Recap fire safety comprehension strategies used.
lessons.home_link: Read a fire safety leaflet together if available.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Word Problems, Time, Counting in 2s
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply word problem, time, and counting in 2s skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can solve addition/subtraction word problems.
I can tell the time.
I can count in 2s.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of word problems, time-telling, and counting in 2s.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations covering each skill.
key_questions: How did you solve this problem?
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 8 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.N1/N2/MEA.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising this week's maths skills over the weekend.

lessons.title: Fire Safety Week Recap Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about fire safety and materials learned this week.
success_criteria: I can name a fire-safe material and its use.
I can recall a fire safety rule.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's science and fire safety learning.
lessons.independent_task: Contribute to a class 'Fire Safety' display combining posters, diagrams, and facts from the week.
key_questions: What have we learned about fire safety?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning, preparing for next week's Great Fire of London study — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about fire safety with your family.
